definition: Biorobotics is an interdisciplinary science that combines the fields of biomedical engineering, cybernetics, and robotics to develop new technologies that integrate biology with mechanical systems to develop more efficient communication, alter genetic information, and create machines that imitate biological systems.
details: Biorobotics is an interdisciplinary science that combines the fields of biomedical engineering, cybernetics, and robotics to develop new technologies that integrate biology with mechanical systems to develop more efficient communication, alter genetic information, and create machines that imitate biological systems.

explainer.lead: Biorobotics brings together biomedical engineering, cybernetics, and robotics to connect biological and mechanical systems. It matters because living systems can inspire more capable machines, while engineered systems can provide new ways to interact with biology.

tiers.eli5: Biorobotics is like learning from both animals and machines to build something new. A scientist might study how a leg moves, then design a robot leg that works in a similar way, or connect a mechanical part with a living system.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply biorobotics when developing machines that imitate biological systems or integrate biological and mechanical components, drawing on biomedical engineering, cybernetics, and robotics. The central challenge is making these different systems work together effectively rather than treating a biological resemblance alone as proof of a useful design.
tiers.paperLevel: Biorobotics = an interdisciplinary science combining biomedical engineering, cybernetics, and robotics. Its stated aims are to integrate biology with mechanical systems, improve communication, alter genetic information, and create machines that imitate biological systems.

explainer.example: A team studies how a biological limb moves and uses those findings to build a robotic limb with a similar pattern of movement. The project combines biological study with mechanical design and control rather than simply copying the limb's appearance.

usedIn.name: Biologically inspired robotics
usedIn.detail: Machines are designed to imitate structures or behaviors found in biological systems.

usedIn.name: Biomedical engineering
usedIn.detail: Engineering methods contribute to technologies that connect biological and mechanical systems.

usedIn.name: Cybernetic systems
usedIn.detail: Communication between biological and mechanical components is a central concern.

explainer.intuition: Biology and machines can be treated as parts of one design problem: biology can supply patterns for machines to imitate, and engineering can supply mechanical systems that interact with living systems.
howItWorks: Identify a biological system or a connection between biology and machinery to study.
Combine knowledge from biomedical engineering, cybernetics, and robotics.
Design a technology that either imitates the biological system or integrates biological and mechanical components.
Develop the resulting communication or machine behavior toward the intended goal.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides a shared approach for creating biologically inspired machines and technologies that link living and mechanical systems. Its goals also include more efficient communication and altering genetic information.
misconceptions: Biorobotics is not just the construction of robots that look like people or animals.
